frequency_question: How often does operational or administrative friction prevent the actual implementation of an announced or planned incremental reserve ratio tool?
membership_rule: Includes any formal policy cycle by a major central bank where an incremental or secondary reserve requirement was proposed or scheduled; excludes permanent or routine adjustments to standard, baseline reserve requirements.

cases.name: People's Bank of China RRR adjustments with targeted tranches (2021-2023)
Central Bank of Sri Lanka Statutory Reserve Ratio special tranches (2011)
Bank of Israel Zekelman-era targeted liquidity absorption requirements (2010)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major named instances globally; represents the population of targeted secondary reserve ratio deployments by central banks facing surplus liquidity.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or opaque domestic consultations where policy was floated informally without reaching formal regulatory notification stages.
skeleton: Central bank administrative execution cycles for liquidity tools: 5 identified historical instances of targeted or incremental reserve ratios across emerging and developed markets over the last 30 years, where 5 out of 5 successfully proceeded to implementation without structural friction causing cancellation.
validity_reason: Central banking operational frameworks for reserve management evolve slowly over decades; current RTGS and banking-system linkages remain structurally consistent.
